name: Shopping & money
description: Konbini, shops, and the register script.

cards.tip: ikura (how much) + desu ka. For 'how many' use ikutsu.
i-adjective: takai, takakunai, takakatta. Means both expensive and tall; context decides.
i-adjective. Also a suffix meaning 'easy to': wakariyasui = easy to understand.
iru (to need) + polite negative. irimasen = don't need. The standard polite refusal, with wa marking what is refused.
Same request pattern as omizu o kudasai. fukuro covers the small plastic bag you now pay a few yen for.

cards.en: Shall I heat it up? (konbini staff)
cards.tip: atatameru (to warm up) in polite form + ka. Staff ask this for bento. Reply hai onegaishimasu or daijoubu desu.

cards.ja: レシートはいりません
cards.tip: Same irimasen pattern. reshiito is a loanword; ryoushuusho is the formal receipt for expenses.

cards.ja: ポイントカードはお持ちですか
cards.romaji: pointo kaado wa omochi desu ka
cards.en: Do you have a points card? (staff)
cards.tip: o- + mochi (have) + desu ka is the honorific 'do you have'. Staff-speak you need to recognise, not produce. Answer nai desu or daijoubu desu.

cards.en: I don't have one / There isn't any
cards.tip: Polite negative of aru (to exist, to have). Casual: nai. nai desu is a common softer version.
de = by means of. genkin de, kaado de, basu de (by bus). One particle, many uses.
Same de. Say it as the answer to oshiharai wa? (payment?).
kore (this) + wa + nan (what) + desu ka. nan before d, t, n sounds; nani elsewhere (nani o?).
shichaku (trying on) + dekimasu (can do) + ka. noun + dekimasu ka = can I do X.

cards.ja: もっと大きいのはありますか
cards.romaji: motto ookii no wa arimasu ka
cards.en: Do you have a bigger one?
cards.tip: motto (more) + ookii (big) + no (one, stands in for the noun) + wa arimasu ka. no replaces a noun you have already named.
mite iru = -te form + iru, the 'am doing' form. dake = only. Polite brush-off for staff.
men (exempt) + zei (tax). Same dekimasu ka pattern. You will need your passport.
The yen. Number first: gohyaku en. It is 'yen' in English and 'en' in Japanese.
o- + tsuri. Staff say otsuri desu while handing it back.
